target.title: fix(memory-wiki): skip malformed legacy import-run files in doctor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs-state.ts` parsed each `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file with an unguarded `JSON.parse` inside the bounded-concurrency legacy reader. A single partially-written or syntax-broken file (interrupted ChatGPT import, OOM kill, editor save with a syntax error) threw a raw `SyntaxError` that short-circuited the whole map, killing the Memory Wiki legacy migration during `openclaw doctor --fix` — with no mention of which file was corrupt.

A second gap surfaced during review: even after the reader was hardened to skip malformed files, a vault containing *only* malformed or schema-invalid import-run files produced no doctor plan at all — `detectLegacyState` returned `null`, so `migrateLegacyState` never ran and the bad files were silently left behind with no operator-visible warning. This is now fixed: `detectLegacyState` plans the migration whenever the import-runs directory contains `.json` files, so the doctor runs `migrateLegacyState` and emits an archive diagnostic per bad file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The modern SQLite-backed sibling `listMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` deserializes rows defensively and returns only the ones that parse. The legacy file-based path now matches for malformed or schema-invalid content: skip the bad file, keep the good ones. Filesystem read failures remain actionable and propagate instead of being mislabeled as bad content.

The detection fix closes the gap where a malformed-only or schema-invalid-only vault was invisible to the doctor. `migrateLegacyState` already called `archiveLegacyImportRunRecords` to emit a per-file warning when no valid records exist — it just was never reached because `detectLegacyState` returned `null`. Detection now counts the legacy import-run `.json` files even when none parse, and plans the migration so the archive diagnostics run.

## User Impact

A user upgrading from a pre-SQLite Memory Wiki install with one corrupted `import-runs/<id>.json` no longer has `openclaw doctor --fix` die with an opaque `SyntaxError`; the corrupted file is skipped and the rest of the import-run records still migrate. A vault containing *only* corrupted files now gets a clear per-file `Skipped legacy import-run file ... (malformed or schema-invalid) — not archived. Inspect or delete the file, then re-run \`openclaw doctor --fix\`.` warning instead of silent no-op. Well-formed files are unchanged.


## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` `661cf9644df5ca46582cc02122c86b110f159c3b`. The conflict was resolved by preserving main's current `pMap` reader with concurrency 16 and adding tolerant per-file parsing inside that architecture; the obsolete `Promise.all` implementation was not restored. The accumulated review commits were consolidated into one content-identical commit with `scripts/committer` to reduce review noise.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** (1) A single malformed `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file threw a raw `SyntaxError`, killing the whole Memory Wiki legacy migration pass. (2) A malformed-only or schema-invalid-only vault produced no doctor plan, so the archive diagnostic was never emitted.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v26.5.0, commit `b7bcd3d75f2e02ac27a1954ca310c892bf194f2f` on branch `fix/memory-wiki-import-runs-jsonparse`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `661cf9644df5ca46582cc02122c86b110f159c3b`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-memory-wiki-doctor.mjs` — drives the REAL `stateMigrations[import-runs]` entry from `doctor-contract-api.ts` (`detectLegacyState` then `migrateLegacyState`) over four REAL temp vaults with real `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` files and a real temp state DB. No mocks: real fs, real plugin migration code, real keyed-store context.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — real fs + real migration code + real temp state DB):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-memory-wiki-doctor.mts
  valid-only: planned=true changes=2 warnings=0 remaining=valid.json.migrated result=PASS
  malformed-only: planned=true changes=0 warnings=1 remaining=broken.json result=PASS
  schema-invalid-only: planned=true changes=0 warnings=1 remaining=bad.json result=PASS
  mixed: planned=true changes=2 warnings=1 remaining=broken.json,valid.json.migrated result=PASS
  node=v26.5.0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All four scenarios plan the migration and run it. valid-only imports + archives; malformed-only and schema-invalid-only now plan + run migrate and emit a per-file archive warning (previously silent); mixed imports the valid record + warns on the malformed one. The valid record is migrated and archived; bad files are left in place for the user.
- **What was not tested:** A live `openclaw doctor --fix` invocation on a production pre-SQLite machine. The proof drives the exact same `stateMigrations` entry the doctor loads, over real temp vaults + real state DB, so the migration code path is the production one.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-wiki/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       11 passed (11)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <four changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <four changed files>
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-99422-extensions.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-99422-extension-tests.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/build-all.mjs
(exit 0)
```

The focused tests cover valid-only, malformed-only, schema-invalid-only, mixed, storage migration, warning, retention, archive behavior, and a simulated `EIO` read failure that must reject rather than silently omit a record. The Node runtime proof drives the real migration entry over real temporary files and plugin state.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a corrupted legacy `import-runs/*.json` is now skipped with a per-file warning instead of killing `openclaw doctor --fix`; a malformed-only/schema-invalid-only vault now produces a doctor plan + per-file warnings instead of a silent no-op; well-formed files and the happy path unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched; only the legacy-file read path and detection planning.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - only error handling around an existing JSON.parse of local legacy files.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - internal to the memory-wiki plugin doctor migration; no public API change.
- Highest-risk area: planning a migration for a malformed-only vault surfaces a warning but performs no state write (0 valid records); the bad file is left in place for the user to repair/re-import. Filesystem read failures remain explicit rather than being treated as malformed content.
- Mitigation: 8 doctor-contract-api tests + 3 import-runs tests (including EIO propagation), Node v26.5.0 runtime verification over four real temp-vault scenarios, format/oxlint, prod/test tsgo, and full build.

## CI provenance

The previous exact-head CI failures were inspected from their job logs. Both `check-lint` failures are the same existing upstream `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts:3764` `preserve-caught-error` violation, and both `check-dependencies` failures are the existing upstream dead export `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/types.ts: BrowserRouteHandler`. Neither file is in this PR diff.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

## Conflict-resolution refresh

GitHub mergeability was refreshed after rebasing the original branch onto `upstream/main` `21382b3755fafd7253339b2f3146b8667c5a7bde`. The only real conflict was in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs-state.ts`: current main now uses `pMapSkip` for rejected legacy records. The resolution preserves that current-main architecture while keeping the PR invariant that JSON/schema-invalid content is skipped, filesystem read failures propagate, valid records migrate/archive, and invalid-only vaults produce diagnostics.

Current exact head: `507a615dabb4546169c4961d09d50be0f20a025a`. GitHub API now reports `mergeable: true`; any `behind` indication is ordinary base drift after main advanced during validation, not a conflict.

target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (a private `isInternalCodexMessageTurn` classifier in `message-provider-binding.ts`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 5 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

---

**AI-assisted checklist**
- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description
- [x] Include a concise **Evidence** section with the most useful validation
- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does
- [x] Run a fresh structured autoreview on the current head and address findings — clean after the final provider-binding refactor
- [x] Resolve or reply to bot review conversations after you address them



## Current-main refresh (2026-07-14)

Head: `593ea071df192b29f24332f7ae687f851cec216b`

- Merged upstream `main` through `692cb8dd9b2089555255c58ba5631f832b1b0c01`; the PR functional diff remains limited to the six Codex app-server files listed below. This refresh includes the upstream fixes for the prior Mattermost and unused-export CI failures.
- Isolated the cross-context provider-binding rule in `message-provider-binding.ts`, rewired all production consumers, and kept its internal classifier private so dependency/dead-code checks do not gain a test-only public surface.
- Real WebChat user turns remain bound to WebChat, while heartbeat, cron, and inter-session turns drop only the internal WebChat binding; a real delivery channel remains bound.
- Verified the dependency contract directly against OpenAI Codex app-server source at `1f0566d3f59298d1bb88820a0d35294f1eeb07ea`: dynamic tool calls carry thread/turn/call/tool/arguments, not an OpenClaw channel/provider binding, so this routing decision belongs in the OpenClaw bridge.

Validation:

- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, scoped production-LOC ratchet, and fresh post-refresh autoreview passed with no actionable findings.

target.title: fix(agents): forward agent/session/run identity to tool-result middleware
target.body:
Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
$ # Shape before vs after (mirrors factory construction)
BEFORE {"runtime":"openclaw"}
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts
 ✓ |agents-core| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 ✓ |agents-embedded-agent| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Regression tests assert `createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner` is called
with the full identity object (and falls back to `getSessionId()` when
sessionId is omitted).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw tool-result middleware context lacked agent/session/run identity compared with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

The shipped documentation instructed users to run pnpm approve-builds -g after installing OpenClaw globally, but pnpm 11+ explicitly removed this global-mode approval command. This is the narrowest maintainable fix that aligns with current pnpm behavior while keeping the source-checkout approval guidance unchanged.

## User Impact
Users installing OpenClaw via pnpm global install can now successfully complete the installation without encountering an unsupported command error. The installation flow remains straightforward with a single command, and the note explains why the change was made for users upgrading from older pnpm versions.

target.title: refactor(whatsapp): centralize inbound turn admission and history finalization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp's inbound reply path duplicated responsibilities already owned by the channel SDK. It projected ingress access decisions into local fields, reconstructed an ingest/preflight/resolve adapter after the message context and dispatch function were already prepared, mapped the SDK decision back into a turn admission, and finalized group history in the reply dispatcher.

That split ownership made the WhatsApp path harder to reason about and allowed its admission and history behavior to drift from the shared turn kernel.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refactor makes the SDK's prepared-turn kernel authoritative for WhatsApp:

- The access-control boundary derives the canonical turn admission directly from the full SDK ingress result.
- The public callback envelope retains the safe, redacted ingress decision without exposing the resolved ingress object or its effective allowlists.
- The prepared message context and dispatcher run through `runPreparedInboundReply`; the synthetic channel-event adapter and local decision mapping are removed.
- Group-history ownership is passed through the prepared turn's history options, so the kernel finalizes it only after a successful dispatch turn.
- Broadcast fan-out continues to omit per-agent history and keeps its existing single finalization barrier after all agents finish.
- The deprecated flat-message path constructs its legacy admission directly instead of fabricating an SDK ingress graph that never existed.

## User Impact

Reachable WhatsApp behavior remains the same, but the ownership boundary is now simpler and consistent with other SDK-driven inbound flows. Successful dispatches finalize pending group history whether the reply is silent or visible. Observe-only turns and failed dispatches retain that history, and broadcasts still clear it once rather than once per agent.

`WhatsAppInboundAdmission` no longer carries the unused `senderAccess`, `commandAccess`, and `activationAccess` projections. Its public ingress decision remains redacted.

## Evidence

- `pnpm check:changed`
- `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp`
- Focused coverage for dispatch, observe-only, silent replies, visible replies, dispatch failure, broadcast's single clear, the legacy flat admission path, and ingress redaction
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`

All checks passed. The refactor also removes more code than it adds from both the production path and the change as a whole.

target.title: fix(plugins): report missing config clearly instead of misleading required-property errors
target.body: ## What changed Two validation paths (`validatePluginConfig` in `src/plugins/loader.ts` and config-time validation in `src/config/validation.ts`) used `value ?? {}` / `entry?.config ?? {}` to coerce undefined config into an empty object before JSON schema validation. For plugins with required schema properties (like `serverUrl` and `apiKey`), this produced misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" errors instead of a clear "missing config" message, causing 50+ spurious "invalid config" log lines during gateway startup config-reload cycles. Added `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` guard in the loader that returns a clear "missing config" error when config is undefined and the schema requires properties. Applied the same pattern to config-time validation: when `entry?.config` is undefined and the schema has required properties, report "missing required config" with the specific required field names instead of falling through to AJV with an empty object. ## Why The `?? {}` fallback masked the real problem: when `entry?.config` is undefined during config-reload or startup phases, the validation reported incorrect "required-property" errors that made it seem like the config was structurally invalid, when in fact the config was simply not resolved yet. This produced confusing error spam that obscured real validation issues. ## Real behavior proof **Behavior addressed**: Plugin config validation with required schemas reports "missing config" instead of misleading per-property "must have required property" errors when config is undefined. Valid config still passes correctly. **Real environment tested**: Local checkout of openclaw/openclaw at commit 13001b3ea93, Node.js v22.22.0, Linux x64 **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 1. Checked `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` against schema with `required: ["serverUrl", "apiKey"]` → returns `true` 2. Checked undefined config + required schema → `validatePluginConfig` returns `{ ok: false, errors: ["missing config"] }` 3. Checked undefined config + empty schema → passes correctly 4. Checked valid config `{ serverUrl: "https://x.com", apiKey: "secret" }` + required schema → passes correctly **Evidence after fix**: Direct node evaluation terminal output confirming all three scenarios: ``` Test 1 (undefined + required): {"ok":false,"errors":["missing config"]} Test 2 (undefined + empty): {"ok":true} Test 3 (defined + required): {"ok":true} ``` **Observed result after fix**: Undefined config with required-property schema produces clear "missing config" error instead of misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" per-property errors. Valid config passes validation correctly. Empty schemas still accept undefined config as before. **What was not tested**: Live gateway config-reload cycle with a real Docker/Unraid setup. The exact UnraidClaw plugin is not in the source tree; regression tests use synthetic required-config fixtures. Fixes #63234

target.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups
target.body:
Closes #106839
Related: #86761

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents running on the Claude CLI runtime with subscription-only auth (Claude Code OAuth, no Anthropic API key) would have every active-memory recall either fail with a billing rejection (no extra-usage balance) or **silently draw paid metered extra usage** (extra usage enabled) — while main-session turns correctly ran on plan limits through the CLI backend. Anthropic routing direct anthropic-messages calls on subscription tokens to extra-usage billing is long-standing behavior; the embedded runner's direct-API passthrough (`cli_runtime_passthrough_openclaw`) was never a viable path for these credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `RunEmbeddedAgentParams.cliBackendDispatch: "subscription-auth"`: when the run's provider is `claude-cli` — directly or via a canonical `anthropic/<model>` ref whose configured `agentRuntime` is claude-cli — a backend is registered, and the ordered credential selection resolves to subscription (oauth/token) or nothing rather than an API key, the run executes through `runCliAgent` as a one-shot turn. Active-memory recall opts in. The dispatch preserves the embedded run's contracts:

- **Tool restriction is enforced server-side**: `toolsAllow` maps to the selectable-backend surface, bounds the loopback MCP grant (tools outside it can be neither listed nor called, even under bypass permission modes), and restricted runs get an exclusive loopback-only MCP bundle — user/plugin MCP servers are not merged in.
- **Transcript parity**: the run is mirrored into the caller-owned session file (user turn, live tool call/result records, assistant snapshot — flushed immediately on abort), so `persistTranscripts`, timeout partial-text salvage, and the live terminal-search watcher work identically to embedded runs.
- **Isolation**: fresh CLI process per run, no live-session reuse, session-scoped MCP cleanup (never the process-wide loopback server), CLI session bindings dropped from the result.
- **Scope**: claude-cli only; `google-gemini-cli` and custom backends keep the passthrough — their direct-API contracts were not verified and this PR makes no claims about them. An available API key keeps the existing fast passthrough. The core-side provider set could move to a `CliBackendConfig` capability flag if maintainers prefer that seam.

## User Impact

Subscription-only Claude CLI deployments get working active-memory recall on plan limits, consistent with their main turns — instead of failing every turn or silently consuming paid extra usage. Setups with an Anthropic API key see no behavior change. No config changes required; note that CLI-dispatched recalls measured 13.8–16.9s on a dev laptop, so the plugin's default 15s `timeoutMs` is tight — 30s is comfortable.

## Evidence

**Current-head success (read this first):** on PR head `a284cb958d` (rebased onto main `4bff6b188e`) (rebased onto current `main`, dist rebuilt from that exact SHA), a live subscription-only recall with the **default plugin config** (no `timeoutMs` override) completes end-to-end:

```
# "Copperfin staging dashboard runs on port 4173; Copperfin launch review meeting was moved to Thursday 10:00 (per 2026-07-12 note)."
# timeoutMs=45000 above is selected by the runner's own dispatch eligibility, not a route-only check.
```

`timeoutMs=45000` is the new CLI-runtime default applied from unset config; `status=ok` with a grounded, cited summary is the successful default-config recall the review asked for. Details, the deny-path proof, and earlier rounds follow.

Before (subscription-only claude-cli setup): every recall fails in under a second, with the recall session recording the direct `anthropic-messages` route.

target.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw config validate` output shows confusing dot-notation paths like `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, omits the actual bad value, and provides no source line number to help users find and fix config errors quickly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three improvements to config validation error messages:
- **Bracket notation** for array indices: `agents.list[3]` instead of `agents.list.3`
- **Received value hints**: appends `, got: "none"` when safe (sensitive paths and secret refs are never leaked)
- **Source line numbers**: prefixes with `openclaw.json:376 --` when the value can be resolved in raw config text

This supersedes #104935 (VectorPeak) which only adds bracket notation without line numbers or received values. Our implementation adds all three features with a compact JSON5 navigator (~300 lines) that handles comments, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, and trailing commas.

Key design decisions:
- Internal `formatConfigPath()` is unchanged -- display-layer enrichment only
- No Zod schema changes, no config parsing changes, no dependency changes
- Reuses existing `isSensitiveConfigPath()` and `isSecretRef()` for safety
- No explicit `$include` detection -- the navigator simply fails silently for paths in included files
- `resolveSegmentsAgainstParsed()` correctly distinguishes array indices from numeric record keys (e.g. `plugins.entries.123` stays as a string key)

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw config validate` now see:
```
- openclaw.json:376 -- agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full"), got: "minimal"
```

Instead of:
```
- agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full")
```

Sensitive paths (tokens, API keys) never show received values. Paths in `$include`d files gracefully degrade to the old format.

## Evidence

### Real CLI Proof

Executed from PR head `b69ca92` with Node v24.18.0, using the live config snapshot on this machine.

**Array bracket notation + line number + received value (safe):**
```
- openclaw.json:376 -- agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full"), got: "minimal"
```

**Sensitive path (no value leak):**
```
- channels.telegram.botToken: Invalid token format
```

**Path in `$include`d file (graceful degradation):**
```
- models.providers.openai.apiKey: Invalid API key format
```

**Numeric record key preserved (not treated as array index):**
```
- openclaw.json:4 -- plugins.entries.123.config.mode: Invalid input (allowed: "good"), got: "bad"
```

### Automated Validation

- [x] Typecheck passes: `pnpm tsgo:core` -- clean
- [x] Core tests pass: 162/162 across 3 changed test files
  - `src/config/issue-location.test.ts` -- 26 tests (navigator, path formatting, value resolution, safety)
  - `src/config/issue-format.test.ts` -- 6 tests (location prefix formatting)
  - `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` -- 130 tests (integration with real snapshot)

Note: `pnpm build` fails on this fork due to pre-existing `[UNRESOLVED_ENTRY]` errors for extension files that don't exist in this fork -- not related to this change. The core typecheck (`tsgo:core`) passes clean.

### Competing PR

PR #104935 (VectorPeak) covers bracket notation only, without line numbers or received values. This PR supersedes it with all three features from the original issue #104854.

_AI-assisted: implementation by Luci (OpenClaw agent) with human review._

Closes #104854

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** comparison: `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads), head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script is run inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). The configured pattern is `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, and `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay; `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>

  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"

  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(perplexity): send Search API date filters with official field names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who run Perplexity web search with `date_after` or `date_before` would not get the requested published-date filtering on the native Perplexity Search API path.

OpenClaw exposes `date_after` and `date_before` as user-facing web search parameters. Those values are validated and converted from `YYYY-MM-DD` into Perplexity's expected `M/D/YYYY` date format, but the final native Search API request used the wrong JSON field names:

- `search_after_date`
- `search_before_date`

Perplexity's Search API documents the fields as:

- `search_after_date_filter`
- `search_before_date_filter`

Example before this change:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

OpenClaw correctly validated the date range and converted it to Perplexity-style dates, but the outbound request body used non-contract field names:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "max_results": 5,
  "search_after_date": "1/1/2024",
  "search_before_date": "6/30/2024"
}
```

That means users asking for a bounded Perplexity search could receive an API validation error or unbounded results instead of results constrained to the requested publication window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Perplexity native Search API request body now uses the documented date-filter fields while preserving OpenClaw's existing user-facing `date_after` / `date_before` parameter names.

The request body construction is kept local to the Perplexity provider runtime and reused by the existing Search API dispatch path. This keeps the fix scoped to the provider-owned API mapping and does not add configuration, SDK surface, new provider behavior, or any OpenRouter/chat-completions compatibility changes.

The OpenRouter and Perplexity chat-completions path is intentionally unchanged. OpenClaw already rejects Search API-only filters on that path with explicit user-facing errors.

## User Impact

Users can now rely on Perplexity native Search API date filters to constrain results by publication date.

This matters for workflows such as:

- searching only releases or announcements published in a specific window
- excluding stale search results when investigating recent behavior
- comparing search results before and after a product or dependency change
- running date-bounded research prompts through OpenClaw's web search tool

The visible user-facing parameters remain the same:

```json
{
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

Only the provider-facing Perplexity request body changes.

## Evidence

Source and contract evidence:

- OpenClaw's Perplexity provider advertises `date_after` and `date_before` for the native Search API path: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.ts`
- The runtime validates `date_after` / `date_before`, rejects invalid ranges, and converts ISO dates through `isoToPerplexityDate`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Before this change, the Perplexity native Search API body used `search_after_date` and `search_before_date`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Perplexity's official Search API reference documents `search_after_date_filter` and `search_before_date_filter`: https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/search-post

Focused regression test added:

- `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts` verifies the native Search API request body maps converted dates to:
  - `search_after_date_filter`
  - `search_before_date_filter`
- The test also proves the existing user-facing date format conversion remains compatible with the provider-facing `M/D/YYYY` values.

Validation run:

```bash
OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 28.97s
```

Additional check:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Result: passed with no whitespace errors.

Remote Testbox note:

`node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json` was attempted first, but the local Crabbox wrapper failed its basic binary sanity check with `selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks`. Per the repository testing guidance, the proof above uses the narrow local fallback for this single touched test file.

target.title: docs(slack): clarify group DM bot membership
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a docs gap where Slack users can read the `dm.groupEnabled` and
`dm.groupChannels` settings and reasonably assume those settings can make
OpenClaw see an existing group DM after someone mentions the bot.

Slack group DMs (MPDMs) do not work that way: if the app is not already a
member of the MPDM, Slack does not deliver the conversation to the app.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Slack docs subsection explaining that `@YourBot` in an existing
group DM does not add the app or make the MPDM visible to it. It also clarifies
that `dm.groupEnabled` and `dm.groupChannels` only filter MPDMs Slack already
delivers, and it links that explanation from the channel config reference.

The documented workarounds are the Slack-supported paths: convert the group DM
to a private channel and invite the app, or have the app open a new MPDM with
`conversations.open`.

## User Impact

Operators get a clearer answer when Slack group-DM routing appears broken: no
OpenClaw config can grant visibility into an MPDM the app never joined. The docs
now point users to the two working setup paths instead of leaving them to chase
`dm.groupEnabled` / `dm.groupChannels` as a fix.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted docs PR prepared by Codex, with a Claude Foreman Opus review pass
  before push.
- Docs-only change.
- Ran `pnpm docs:list` before editing docs.
- Ran `pnpm check:docs`:
  - `format:docs:check`
  - `lint:docs`
  - `docs:check-mdx`
  - `docs:check-i18n-glossary`
  - `docs:check-links`
  - `docs:map:check`
- Regenerated `docs/docs_map.md` with `pnpm docs:map:gen`.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Verified the public diff contains no private Slack channel IDs, local project
  paths, or security-advisory details.
- Reviewed by Claude Foreman on Opus before push. Foreman flagged the original
  workaround wording as too broad, so the final text now uses the narrower
  documented bot-token `conversations.open` path.

target.title: fix(discord): bound stalled probe response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord probe checks could hang after the `getMe` request returned response headers but the JSON response body stopped producing data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord probe now reads the successful `getMe` JSON body through the bounded response reader with the existing 16 MiB cap and a per-chunk timeout tied to the probe timeout. Application metadata reads are also bounded, and the status entry point carries only the remaining caller timeout through cold lazy loading. Existing non-OK handling, malformed JSON wording, and the already-resolved bot result are preserved.

## User Impact

Discord configuration checks now return from stalled response bodies instead of waiting indefinitely. If optional application metadata stalls, the successful bot identity remains available.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/probe.intents.test.ts extensions/discord/src/channel.test.ts extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts` (`3` files, `63` tests passed)
- `git diff --check b0ebb81e89f5217397d409c996e2bbf914623a94..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings

## Proof

### Exact-current-head controlled local HTTP production-path proof

Exact head: `3a470fcd81a815982a1669c4568518bb75551331`.

Command:

```text
git rev-parse HEAD
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u all_proxy timeout 30s ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --no-cache scratchpad/discord-probe-current-head-proof.ts
```

The temporary harness called the production `discordPlugin.status.probeAccount()` and `probeDiscord()` paths. It used a real loopback `node:http` server and real Node `fetch`; the existing fetch seam only rewrote the fixed Discord origin to loopback while forwarding the production request options and abort signal. No mocked `Response`, Discord traffic, or credentials were used.

Redacted transcript:

```text
3a470fcd81a815982a1669c4568518bb75551331
proof=controlled-local-http production-path=discord-status+probe
cold-status-app-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=undefined elapsed=290ms callerBudget=300ms socketAborted=true
normal ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=7ms
get-me-stall ok=false error="discord.probe.getMe: JSON response stalled after 140ms" elapsed=188ms socketAborted=true
recovery-after-get-me-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=6ms
application-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=undefined elapsed=200ms callerBudget=220ms socketAborted=true
final-recovery ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=6ms
requests=11 assertions=passed
```

Observed:

- The first status probe in the process cold-loaded the lazy probe runtime. A partial application-metadata body then stalled, was aborted, and returned in `290ms` within the `300ms` caller budget; the resolved bot identity remained present and optional application metadata was omitted.
- A partial `getMe` JSON body that stopped producing bytes returned the production idle-timeout error and closed the server response before `writableEnded` (`socketAborted=true`).
- A direct stalled application-metadata response also closed before `writableEnded`, returned inside the `220ms` caller budget, and preserved `ok=true` plus the bot identity.
- Normal probes before and after the failures returned both bot and application data, demonstrating later-call recovery. All harness assertions passed with exit `0`.

Known limits: this is controlled local real-HTTP production-path proof, not live Discord. It does not claim live Discord behavior or credentialed testing. The `getMe` body protection is an idle/per-chunk timeout, not a total response deadline, so this proof covers a body that stops producing data and does not claim protection from an indefinitely slow trickle. The temporary uncommitted harness was removed after the run.


This exact-head section supersedes the earlier `f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457` transcript.

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-08 JST / 2026-07-07 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@623534400684eca7c451cf587189fae714f2abe2` into the PR branch. The merge conflicted in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`; resolved by keeping main's pre-connect send-evidence cleanup and this PR's no-budget reconciliation-deferral path/tests.
- Follow-up main refresh in the same run: `origin/main` advanced again to `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; merged it with no conflicts and pushed final head `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready with head `1779a704bc1b3a9e7b57e994fea534fac68c2eec`, base `a7c4a0471d944e3c3bf2b3071a5b1b485548dc8d`, `mergeable=CONFLICTING` via GraphQL, and the local branch was 378 commits behind `origin/main`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`, base is `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; GitHub CI is pending on the refreshed head and `reviewDecision` remains empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- Current-head refresh validation:
  - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` was attempted locally after the conflicted merge, but the infra Vitest runner produced no test output for 150s and was interrupted; the narrower recovery-file run also produced no test output for 120s and was interrupted. This hang was root-caused and fixed in the follow-up below.
  - Functional PR diff remains scoped to 7 files: 2 source, 4 tests, 1 docs; 293 insertions / 36 deletions.

## Follow-up (2026-07-09): infra shard hang, replay-pacing skip, and summary counters

Fixed in `1ab8620ebfc43fef70dbf258e3888338bcd704ec` (`fix(outbound): skip replay pacing for unreconcilable deferrals`).

- Root cause of the CI/local hang: `recoverPendingDeliveries` awaited `recoveryReplayPacer.wait(deadline)` (a real `sleep`) *before* `drainQueuedEntry` for every eligible entry, including ambiguous rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter that only defer. Under the recovery test's fake timers (`delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts:574`, "rechecks deferred ambiguous entries after the backoff elapses"), the pacer's `lastReplayStartedAt` equalled the frozen clock, so `wait()` scheduled a `RECOVERY_REPLAY_SPACING_MS` `sleep` that was never advanced. That deadlocked the module-singleton pacer mutex (`waitQueue`), which then hung every later test that paced. The merge that surfaced it advanced `origin/main` to `7ff3f2dbf922`; the pacing feature landed on the branch across the same range.
- Fix: resolve reconciliation availability (cheap adapter/`reconcileUnknownSend` capability check) before the pacer in both `recoverPendingDeliveries` and `drainPendingDeliveries`. No-reconciler ambiguous rows now defer as a no-op — they no longer pay the 250ms send-replay spacing or eat the 60s `maxRecoveryMs` deadline (addresses the 2026-07-07 Codex review). Entries that actually reconcile or replay pace exactly as before.
- Reporting: the no-reconciler deferral now increments a distinct `deferredNoReconciler` summary counter and log clause instead of being reported as a delivery failure, so operator logs match the persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0` state.
- Validation (local, current head `1ab8620`):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts` — previously hanging shard now completes: **260 files, 4303 passed, 3 skipped, 156s**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts` — 4 files, 78 passed (adds a focused case proving a no-reconciler deferral consumes no pacer budget).
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` — clean.
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` — clean.
- Current-head GitHub CI after push: pending on the new head, including Real behavior proof and normal CI/security guard buckets.
- Previous scoped validation for the functional changes, before this main refresh:
  - `node scripts/docs-list.js`
  - `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`
    - 4 files passed, 69 tests passed.
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
    - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence (captured before the 2026-07-09 counter fix, so the summary still reports the no-reconciler deferral as `1 failed`; see note below):

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 1 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":1,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0}
deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

Note — this evidence predates commit `1ab8620`. The queue/state observations (no `deliver` call, one pending entry, `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`) are unchanged, but the summary and log now classify the no-reconciler deferral correctly. After the fix the same scenario reports:

```text
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff), 1 deferred (no reconciler)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":0,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0,"deferredNoReconciler":1}
```

This corrected behavior is asserted deterministically by `delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` (e.g. "keeps entries abandoned after platform send may have started pending without reconciliation" and the new "does not spend replay pacing on unavailable-reconciler deferrals" case). The terminal proof was not re-run on this machine because it hosts a production gateway; the recovery path's real `resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter(allowBootstrap: true)` bootstrap does not terminate in a bare non-gateway `tsx` process, so the deterministic Vitest coverage is the authoritative post-fix evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

`packages/ai` ships without a `scripts.build` field and was not added to the `tsdown.config.ts` `configs` array. After `pnpm build` completes successfully, `packages/ai/dist/` is never produced. This causes `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` when the gateway or bundled plugins try to `import('@openclaw/ai')`, resulting in crash loops on fresh installs and upgrades.
- Problem: `@openclaw/ai` (extracted from `llm-runtime` in PR #99059) has no tsdown build config entry; `pnpm build` silently skips it.
- Solution: Add a `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig("ai", ...)` entry with a custom `buildAiDistEntries()` function that maps all 6 public exports and 7 internal modules to their source paths.
- What changed: `tsdown.config.ts` (+21 lines) — added `buildAiDistEntries()` function and `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig("ai", { entry: ... })` config entry.
- What did NOT change: No package.json changes, no source file changes, no build script changes; only the shared tsdown config array was extended.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening

## Linked Issue/PR

## Motivation

PR #99059 (`062f88e3e3a`, 2026-07-05) extracted `@openclaw/ai` from `llm-runtime`. The migration deleted the old `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig("llm-runtime")` entry from `tsdown.config.ts` but never added a replacement `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig("ai")` entry. The `TSDOWN_PACKAGE_NAMES` list in `scripts/lib/tsdown-output-roots.mjs` includes `"ai"` (for stale-output cleanup), confirming the omission is accidental. The `buildPackageDistEntriesFromExports` helper cannot be used for `ai` because the `./internal/*` wildcard export resolves to an invalid `*.ts` glob entry. A custom `buildAiDistEntries` function is required, following the same pattern as `buildLlmCoreDistEntries`, `buildAgentCoreDistEntries`, and `buildSpeechCoreDistEntries`.

- Behavior addressed: `packages/ai/dist/` is now produced by `pnpm tsdown`; `import('@openclaw/ai')` resolves correctly.

target.title: fix: preserve Codex quota when status uses default runtime
target.body:
Closes #105184

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server users would lose the usage/quota line from `/status` when the session still used the `codex` provider but the displayed runtime fell back to OpenClaw Default. The line could also remain absent when a separate rate-limit read did not inherit the active session's ChatGPT authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat `provider=codex` as authoritative for synthetic Codex usage and resolve its status/auth lookup through the OpenAI profile path even when the displayed harness is the default runtime. Rate-limit reads reuse the auth-matched shared app-server client and fall back only to that exact physical client's recent rate-limit cache when the live read fails, preventing quota data from crossing agent, profile, or client boundaries.

## User Impact

Codex app-server users can continue to see their remaining quota in chat `/status` and CLI status output after the runtime label falls back to OpenClaw Default. A transient quota read failure can use a recent snapshot already owned by the active Codex client instead of silently dropping the usage line.

target.title: fix(android): stop killing long chat runs with hardcoded timeouts (#106863)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Any agent turn longer than ~2 minutes started from the Android app ends in an error, while the identical turn over Telegram completes fine. Full analysis in #106863. Two independent causes, both in `ChatController.kt`:

1. `buildChatSendParams` hardcodes `timeoutMs: 30_000` into every `chat.send`. The gateway uses that as the server-side run expiry (`resolveAgentTimeoutMs({ cfg, overrideMs: p.timeoutMs })` in `chat-send-session.ts`), so the maintenance sweep aborts app-initiated runs that outlive ~30 s + grace ("CLI run aborted" / "Embedded agent failed before reply"). Other channels get the config default (48 h). Queued sends burn their expiry budget before their turn even starts.
2. `armPendingRunTimeout` fires after a hard 120 s, refreshes the history snapshot, computes `runStillInFlight` — and then declares a timeout **even when the run is confirmed in flight**: spurious "Timed out waiting for a reply" banner, optimistic bubble removed, outbox row parked as Failed/delivery-unconfirmed. Streaming deltas never re-arm the timer, so this hits actively streaming turns too.

## Fix

- Omit `timeoutMs` from `chat.send` so app runs get the gateway's configured default expiry, same as other channels.
- In `armPendingRunTimeout`, when the post-delay snapshot confirms the run is still in flight, re-arm the timer and keep waiting instead of timing out. The not-in-flight path is unchanged; terminal events and the server-side expiry remain the liveness backstop, so a genuinely dead run still resolves (and `wasTimedOut` recovery is untouched).

## Evidence

Before/after screen recordings on a real device (Pixel 5, same gateway, same long-running prompt — an agent turn deliberately longer than 2 minutes):

- **Before** (current app): ["Timed out waiting for a reply" at ~120 s, optimistic bubble lost](https://github.com/LeC-D/openclaw/releases/download/pr106864-evidence/before-test.mp4)
- **After** (debug APK built from this PR's head, d50a26f7, via CI `assembleDebug`): [same prompt, no timeout — the run keeps streaming and the reply lands normally](https://github.com/LeC-D/openclaw/releases/download/pr106864-evidence/after-test.mp4)

Both files are hosted as release assets on the fork: <https://github.com/LeC-D/openclaw/releases/tag/pr106864-evidence>

Additional verification:

- Verified the equivalent server-side behavior on a live gateway (Android/Termux host where turns of 2–11+ min are routine): with the 30 s override neutralized, app-initiated long turns complete exactly like Telegram ones instead of ~50% dying to run expiry.
- `ChatControllerReconnectRestoreTest` updated for the re-armed timer (perpetual-job pattern on `backgroundScope`); `android-test-play` and `android-test-third-party` are green on the current head.

Fixes #106863

target.title: fix(clickclack): redact REST error details
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

- `logging.redactSensitive` is disabled.
- custom `logging.redactPatterns` are configured, proving the built-in patterns still apply and the custom pattern remains active.

target.title: fix: harden cloud worker admission and remote turns
target.body:
Related: #104294

AI-assisted: yes. The complete diff was reviewed with the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where cloud-worker provisioning and remote turns could retain a forbidden lease while waiting for SSH, accept stale worker state, or process malformed and unbounded streamed tool-call data. Those failure modes could leave cloud work running outside the documented credential and network boundary, lose terminal tool-call state, or keep a placement attached after its worker bundle became stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes Crabbox admission fail closed before readiness polling, gives provisioning, setup, and cleanup independent lifecycle budgets, bounds and reconciles streamed tool-call state against the authoritative terminal message, projects provider terminals onto the closed worker protocol, and tears down stale attached placements. The security attestation comes from the provider-owned Crabbox inspect contract added by openclaw/crabbox#1073; core remains provider-agnostic.

Landing dependency: publish Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer through the supported install channels before merging. The latest published release is currently v0.38.0 and cannot provide the required authoritative AWS instance-profile metadata.

## User Impact

Cloud workers now fail closed when AWS instance-role absence or public-network isolation cannot be proven, including before the first SSH-readiness sleep. Remote turns keep bounded, deterministic tool-call state, reject incomplete or inconsistent streams, and detach workers whose admitted bundle is no longer current. Operators need Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer for AWS-backed workers.

## Evidence

- Fresh autoreview: clean after fixing post-end tool-call deltas and malformed-inspect lease cleanup; no accepted or actionable findings remain.
- Exact-head full changed gate: green on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxffdr33xg10d0xytwrhaq7y`, including formatting, SDK baseline, core and extension type checks, lint, database/storage guards, and import-cycle checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29306988236
- Focused inference and Crabbox provider regression suites: 80/80 passing on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxfd2zd0gwv2698d3taeb372`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29305301562
- Deadcode export gate after CI cleanup: green: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29302832058
- Focused worker runtime, placement, service, inference, and provider suites: 186 passing: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29299519873
- Live AWS isolation proof: Node available; ambient model, GitHub, SSH-agent, and AWS credentials absent; IMDS credentials endpoint denied; public npm egress available: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4d611f994b5f
- Live remote turn proof: three distinct nonce-writing tool turns completed, then direct remote reads verified all three artifacts: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_21d25d42ac35
- Final live remote artifact read on the hardened inference path: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_010d97a1a353
- Fault injection: externally releasing the active lease reconciled the placement to reclaimed, destroyed its environment, and prevented a new worker claim.
- Companion Crabbox contract landed in openclaw/crabbox#1073 at 32e9ebca0ee4215cd71d5292004c15e49706af82; full Go and Worker suites passed, and coordinator deployment succeeded: https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29296595939
